statement: For the fixed surface $E\times E$ and embedding considered above, the full Hasse polynomial $h_d(s)=\det M_d(s)$ is geometrically reduced for every $d\ge1$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Frobenius-periodic reflexive sheaves] Let $P$ be projective space over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. If a coherent reflexive sheaf $\mathcal S$ has an isomorphism $F^*\mathcal S\simeq\mathcal S$, then it is a trivial vector bundle with its constant unit-Frobenius structure.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Determinant allocation] Let $P=\mathbf P^m$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, and let $\mathcal E=\Omega_P^1$ carry a generically invertible Frobenius-linear map. Suppose its Hasse divisor is reduced and irreducible. Every nonzero proper invariant subspace of its Lang representation has trivial quotient representation.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [A fixed natural block in every higher degree] For every $d\ge3$, the geometric group on the fixed surface contains a subgroup acting as the natural $\GL_{80}(\mathbf F_2)$ on an $80$-dimensional direct summand and trivially on a complementary summand.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Conditional exact uniform product groups] Fix $d\ge3$ on the surface $E\times E$ above. If the degree-$d$ Hasse divisor is geometrically irreducible, then both geometric and arithmetic groups are \[ \begin{cases} \GL_{9d^2-1}(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ odd},\\ \mathbf F_2^{\,3(9d^2-4)}\rtimes\GL_{9d^2-4}(\mathbf F_2), &d\text{ even}, \end{cases} \] where in the second line the group is the full pointwise stabilizer of the three known independent covectors. Theorem~\ref{thm:product-Hasse-irred} below proves the required geometric irreducibility for every $d\ge4$, thereby completing the entire fixed-surface full-image problem together with the three certified initial degrees.
depends_on: KantorSeress2001; lem:irreducible-hasse-quotients-trivial; lem:product-degree-three-block; prop:product-hasse-reduced; thm:product-Hasse-irred; thm:product-all-degree-transvections; thm:product-char2-all-parities-fixed-quotient; thm:product-char2-two-full-groups
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Why reducedness alone was insufficient] Generic stable loss one proves reducedness, but does not by itself exclude two reduced components meeting in codimension two. The subsequent proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:product-Hasse-irred} supplies the missing irreducibility by mixed tacnodal unions and smooth points joining all restriction factors. It does not assume a generic symmetric-matrix rank bound for the special Cartier matrices.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [A pointed Cartier calculation] Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve in characteristic two with one-dimensional Cartier kernel, generated by $\omega$. If $P\in C$ satisfies $\omega(P)\ne0$, then Cartier induces a surjection \[ H^0(C,\omega_C(2P))\longrightarrow H^0(C,\omega_C), \] and its kernel is $k\omega$. If $D$ is ordinary, the corresponding map for $D$ is surjective with a one-dimensional kernel, whose nonzero members have a nonzero double-pole coefficient at $P$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Smoothness at a mixed tacnodal union] Let $X=E\times E$ be the fixed ordinary surface above. Let $C\in|L^a|$ and $D\in|L^e|$ be smooth curves without common components, ordinary except that $C$ has a one-dimensional Cartier kernel $k\omega$. Suppose they have a single simple tangency at $P$, are otherwise transverse, and $\omega(P)\ne0$. Then the full degree-$(a+e)$ Hasse divisor is smooth at $C\cup D$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [The degree-one jet exception is small] On the fixed product, $L^e$ for $e\ge2$ separates second jets at one point and first jets at any two distinct points. For $L$ itself, second jets are separated at a point $P=(P_1,P_2)$ when neither $P_i$ is a flex in its plane cubic. For every $Q\ne P$, the joint first-jet evaluation has rank at least five; for fixed $P$, rank six fails only on the two fibres through $P$ and a finite set of other points.
depends_on: Self-contained proof in the indicated section
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Uniform Hasse irreducibility] For the fixed surface and embedding, the degree-$d$ Hasse divisor is geometrically irreducible for every $d\ge4$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [All full groups on the fixed ordinary product] Let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic two, let \[ E:\ Y^2Z+XYZ+X^3+Z^3=0,\qquad X=E\times E,\qquad L=\mathcal O_E(3O)\boxtimes\mathcal O_E(3O), \] and use the fixed Segre embedding. For every $d\ge1$, the maximal relative Hasse--Witt rank is $r_d=9d^2-1$. On the smooth ordinary degree-$d$ hypersurface-section open, the entire geometric and arithmetic images coincide and are \[ G_{{\rm geom},d}=G_{{\rm arith},d}= \begin{cases} \GL_{9d^2-1}(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ odd},\\[2mm] \left\{\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\0&I_3\end{pmatrix}: A\in\GL_{9d^2-4}(\mathbf F_2),\quad B\in M_{(9d^2-4)\times3}(\mathbf F_2)\right\},&d\text{ even}. \end{cases} \] In even degree this is exactly the pointwise stabilizer of all three independent invariant covectors, and its order is $2^{3(9d^2-4)}|\GL_{9d^2-4}(\mathbf F_2)|$. The representation is irreducible exactly in odd degree.

statement: [A universal elliptic Cartier symmetrizer] Let $E:y^2+xy=x^3+A x^2+B$ over a perfect field of characteristic two, with $B\ne0$, and put $N=\mathcal O_E(3O)$. In the basis $(1,x,y)$ and with the Cartier-invariant differential $\eta=dx/x$, the root-removed Cartier multiplication matrix is \[ M(s)=\begin{pmatrix} s_0&B s_2&B s_1\\ s_2&s_1+A s_2&s_0+A s_1\\ 0&s_2&s_1+s_2 \end{pmatrix}. \] The constant invertible matrix \[ R=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&B\\0&0&B\\0&B&(1+A)B\end{pmatrix}, \qquad\det R=B^2, \] satisfies \[ RM(s)=\begin{pmatrix} s_0&0&B s_2\\ 0&B s_2&B(s_1+s_2)\\ B s_2&B(s_1+s_2)&B s_0+B s_1+(1+A)B s_2 \end{pmatrix}. \] Thus $RM(s)$ is symmetric and its diagonal is $R^t s$. For any pair of ordinary elliptic curves with degree-three line bundles, the analogous nine-dimensional Cartier pencil has a constant invertible symmetrizer and an invertible linear map to its nine diagonal entries.

statement: [An explicit nonreduced relative Hasse divisor] The relative coherent Frobenius bundle is $\mathcal E=\Omega^1_P$. A smooth generic section has genus ten and $2$-rank eight.

statement: [A first-derivative criterion for wild transvection inertia] Let $R=k[[t]]$ with $k$ algebraically closed of characteristic two, and let a rank-$r$ vector bundle over $R$ have regular semilinear Frobenius $F$. Let $u$ generate the semilinear kernel in the special fibre, and let $v$ be the first derivative of $F(\widetilde u)$ at $t=0$, for a regular lift $\widetilde u$. If $v\notin ku$, the generic Lang local system has a nontrivial transvection in its inertia.

statement: Let $(A,\Theta)$ be a principally polarized abelian variety of dimension $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic two, and let $L=\mathcal O_A(3\Theta)$ and $W=H^0(A,L)$. statement: [Eventual exact images for all ordinary principally polarized surfaces] Let $(A,\Theta)$ be an ordinary principally polarized abelian surface over any perfect field $k$ of characteristic two, with a line bundle representing $\Theta$ over $k$, and embed it by $L=\mathcal O_A(3\Theta)$. After a finite extension of $k$, there exists an odd polarized isogeny $\phi:A'\to A$ with multiplier $n$ whose source has degree-one relative geometric group $\GL_8(\mathbf F_2)$. For the complete systems $|L^d|$, put $d_1=n+1$. For the ambient hypersurface systems of this fixed embedding, replace it by \[ d_1=\max\{n+1,\operatorname{reg}(\mathcal I_A)-1\}. \] For every $d\ge d_1$, put $r=9d^2-1$. If $d$ is odd, the entire geometric and arithmetic images both equal $\GL_r(\mathbf F_2)$. If $d$ is even, put $N=r-3$ and let $\Gamma\subset S_3$ be the actual Galois image permuting the three nonzero characters of $\ker F_A$. After compatible choices of bases the entire images are \[ G_{{\rm geom},d}= \left\{\begin{pmatrix}B&T\\0&I_3\end{pmatrix}: B\in\GL_N(\mathbf F_2),\ T\in M_{N\times3}(\mathbf F_2)\right\}, \] \[ G_{{\rm arith},d}= \left\{\begin{pmatrix}B&T\\0&\gamma\end{pmatrix}: B\in\GL_N(\mathbf F_2),\ T\in M_{N\times3}(\mathbf F_2),\ \gamma\in\Gamma\right\}, \] where $\Gamma$ acts by its three-dimensional permutation matrices. The representation is irreducible exactly in odd degree. The integer $n$, and hence the threshold, can be found by a terminating procedure over finite fields or effectively presented finitely generated fields of definition; over arbitrary perfect fields the statement gives existence without presupposing computable coefficients.

statement: [The four-parameter alternating theta tensor] Work over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. Index a nine-dimensional space $W$ by the points of $I=\mathbf F_3^2$, and let $\mathcal D=\mathbf P^1(\mathbf F_3)$ be its four line directions. For $i\in\mathcal D$ put \[ P_i(s)=\sum_{\substack{\ell\subset I\text{ affine line}\\ \operatorname{dir}(\ell)=i}} \prod_{a\in\ell}s_a, \qquad P_*(s)=\sum_{a\in I}s_a^3. \] Let $T$ be the alternating trilinear form whose value on three distinct basis vectors is $\alpha_i$ when their indices form a line of direction $i$, and zero otherwise. Let $M(s)$ be its contraction matrix: \[ M(s)_{ab}=T(s,e_b,e_a). \] Then $M(s)s=0$, and the vector of its eight-by-eight principal Pfaffians is $q_\alpha(s)s$, where \begin{equation} q_\alpha(s)= \left(\prod_{i\in\mathcal D}\alpha_i\right)P_*(s) +\sum_{i\in\mathcal D} \alpha_i\left(\sum_{j\ne i}\alpha_j^3\right)P_i(s). \end{equation} Consequently \[ \operatorname{adj}M(s)=q_\alpha(s)^2ss^t. \] For a nonzero coefficient vector $\alpha$, the cubic $q_\alpha$ vanishes identically precisely in either of the following cases: exactly one coefficient is nonzero; or exactly three are nonzero and their cubes are equal. These are forty points in the projective coefficient space. In each case $W$ is a direct sum of three three-dimensional spaces on which $T$ is the sum of three nonzero volume forms. In particular it has a nontrivial projector $D$ with \[ T(Ds,t,u)=T(s,Dt,u). \]

statement: [The ordinary Frobenius algebra and its two pencils] Let $E$ be an ordinary elliptic curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, let $F:E\to E'=E^{(2)}$ be relative Frobenius, and let $H=\OO_{E'}(qO)$, where $q\ge3$. There is an orthogonal decomposition \[ F_*\OO_E=\OO_{E'}\oplus B,\qquad B\not\simeq\OO_{E'},\qquad \mu:B^{\otimes2}\xrightarrow{\sim}\OO_{E'}. \] Here orthogonality refers to the multiplication--Cartier pairing, normalized to take the value one on $(1,1)$; in this decomposition the pairing is $(a,b),(c,d)\mapsto ac+\mu bd$. Put $V=F_*F^*H=H\oplus HB$. One can choose $a_0\in H^0(H)$ and $b_2\in H^0(HB)$ with reduced, disjoint zero divisors $A$ and $D$. For every such choice the following maps are isomorphisms: \[ \begin{split} H^0(H)\oplus H^0(HB)&\longrightarrow H^0(H^2),\\ (x,y)&\longmapsto a_0x+\mu b_2y,\\ H^0(HB)&\longrightarrow H^0(A,HB|_A),\\ H^0(H)&\longrightarrow H^0(D,H|_D). \end{split} \]

statement: [A toral lattice for the unresolved rank problem] Let $A$ be a mixed abelian surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. Let $N$ be ample and suppose its ordinary polarization index is positive. Put $b=h^0(A,N)$ and $P=\mathbf P(H^0(A,N))$. Then $b$ is even. There is a normalized toral invariant derivation $e$, acting on $N$, for which \[ W=H^0(A,N)=W_0\oplus W_1,\qquad e|W_i=i,\qquad\dim W_0=\dim W_1=b/2. \] Write $\mathcal B=W^*\otimes\mathcal O_P(-1)$ and \[ Z=\mathbf P(W_0)\cup\mathbf P(W_1),\qquad \mathcal I=\ker\bigl(\mathcal B \xrightarrow{(s,es)}\mathcal O_P^2\bigr). \] Outside $Z$, the sheaf $\mathcal I$ is locally free of rank $b-2$. If $b/2\ge2$, its reflexive extension has $\det\mathcal I=\mathcal O_P(-b)$ and $H^0(P,\mathcal I)=0$. The full coherent Frobenius maps into $\mathcal I$ and preserves it. When $N=M^{3d}$, the expected sharp relative rank $b-2$ is equivalent to nonvanishing of the determinant of $F_P^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal I$, a homogeneous form of degree $b$.

statement: [The exact first-variation test] At a point outside $Z$ where the induced map on $\mathcal I$ has corank exactly two, let $K$ and $Q$ be its two-dimensional kernel and cokernel. A tangent direction $t$ gives \[ D_t:K\longrightarrow Q. \] In a local frame the lowest possible term of the determinant along that direction is a nonzero fixed scalar times $\det D_t$. Let $P(s)$ be the rectangular inclusion matrix of a local frame of $\mathcal I$ into $\mathcal B$, and choose a local left inverse $L(s)$, so that $L(s)P(s)=1$. The Frobenius matrix is $L(s)M(s)^tP(s)^{[2]}$. Over dual numbers the derivative of the last factor is zero; the derivative of the first factor vanishes on $K$. Consequently $D_t$ is obtained by restricting $M(t)^t$ and projecting to $Q$. This is a precise sufficient test for a deformation to the sharp-rank open. The next lemma proves the required first-corank statement for an etale double pullback of a sharp positive-index source. Nonvanishing of $\det D_t$ remains unproved in general.

statement: [The restricted first corank at every sharp double pullback] Let $\pi:A\to B$ be an etale double isogeny of mixed abelian surfaces. Let $H$ be ample of positive ordinary index, put $N=\pi^*H$, and use compatible toral lifts on these bundles. Suppose that a section $s\in H^0(B,H)$ makes Frobenius on $I_B=\ker(s,es)\subset H^2(B,H^{-1})$ bijective. Set $s_A=\pi^*s$ and $b=h^0(A,N)$. Then on $I_A=\ker(s_A,es_A)$ the first Frobenius rank and stable Frobenius rank are both $b-4$. Its kernel and cokernel have dimension two. The full coherent first rank need not equal $b-4$. For this point, the first-variation map $D_t$ of the preceding remark vanishes whenever $t$ is pulled back from $H^0(B,H)$. Consequently it factors through the surjective trace map \[ H^0(A,N)\longrightarrow H^0(B,H). \] Thus the remaining sufficient sharpness test is the nonvanishing of a quadratic determinant of a linear map $H^0(B,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(k^2,k^2)$.

statement: [Two-point Cartier obstruction] Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. Let $P\ne Q$ be points, with chosen uniformizers $x_P,x_Q$, and put $A_C=\ker(C:H^0(\omega_C)\to H^0(\omega_C))$. Let $U\subset H^0(\omega_C(2P+2Q))$ be the subspace of forms with zero residues at both points. Taking the double-pole coefficients gives \[ 0\longrightarrow H^0(\omega_C)\longrightarrow U \xrightarrow{\mathrm{pp}}k^2\longrightarrow0. \] Cartier maps $U$ to $H^0(\omega_C)$ and induces a semilinear map \[ \delta:k^2\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker} (C:H^0(\omega_C)\to H^0(\omega_C)). \] Under Serre and finite-Frobenius duality its dual, with the appropriate scalar Frobenius twists, is the evaluation map \[ A_C\longrightarrow k^2, \qquad\eta\longmapsto(\eta(P),\eta(Q)). \] In particular a Cartier-killed form with equal, nonzero double-pole coefficients exists if and only if $\eta(P)+\eta(Q)=0$ for every $\eta\in A_C$.

statement: [Smoothness at a mixed self-tacnode] Let $A',A$ be superspecial abelian surfaces in characteristic two, and let $\phi:A'\to A$ be an odd-degree isogeny. Fix invariant volume forms and identify the invariant one-forms using $\phi^*$. Let $C'\subset A'$ be a smooth ample curve and suppose its image $Z=\phi(C')$ is birationally normalized by $C'$. Assume that $Z$ has ordinary nodes and exactly one simple tacnode, the latter obtained by identifying $P,Q=P+g$ for a nonzero $g\in\ker\phi$. Their tangent lines agree after translation. Choose the same tangent coordinate on these two branches. Assume that \[ \ker C_{C'}= H^0(A',\Omega^1_{A'})|_{C'}\oplus k\eta, \qquad \eta(P)\ne\eta(Q), \] and that $\mathcal N=\mathcal O_A(Z)$ has a separable polarization. Suppose also that $\mathcal N$ is very ample. Then the relative coherent Frobenius on $|\mathcal N|$, on the quotient by ambient $H^1(A,\mathcal O_A)$, has corank one at $Z$, and its determinant has a nonzero first derivative there. Thus the relative Hasse divisor is smooth at $Z$.

statement: [Smoothness at a mixed ordinary triple point] Let $A',A$ be superspecial abelian surfaces in characteristic two, and let $\phi:A'\to A$ be an odd-degree isogeny. Let $C'\subset A'$ be smooth and suppose $\phi|_{C'}$ is birational onto its image $Z$. Assume $Z$ has ordinary nodes and exactly one ordinary triple point, with preimages $P_1,P_2,P_3$. Choose tangent parameters on these three branches such that their tangent vectors, identified by $\phi$, satisfy $v_3=v_1+v_2$. Suppose \[ \ker C_{C'}=H^0(A',\Omega^1_{A'})|_{C'}\oplus k\eta, \qquad \eta(P_1)+\eta(P_2)+\eta(P_3)\ne0, \] where values use the chosen tangent vectors. Suppose $\mathcal N=\mathcal O_A(Z)$ is globally generated and its polarization is separable. Then the relative coherent Cartier map has corank one at $Z$, and its determinant has a nonzero first derivative there. The relative Hasse divisor is therefore smooth at $Z$.

statement: [A negative reflexive extension of the unit image] The space $W$ is a free module of rank $b/4$ over \[ \mathcal A=k[\delta_1,\delta_2]/(\delta_1^2,\delta_2^2). \] Define reflexive sheaves on $P$ by \[ \mathcal I=\ker\bigl(\mathcal B\xrightarrow{(s,\delta_1s,\delta_2s)} \mathcal O_P^3\bigr),\qquad \mathcal K=\ker\bigl(\mathcal B\xrightarrow{ (s,\delta_1s,\delta_2s,\delta_1\delta_2s)}\mathcal O_P^4\bigr). \] Let $Z_0\subset P$ be the linear locus $\delta_1\delta_2s=0$. It has codimension $b/4$. On $P^\circ=P\setminus Z_0$ these are vector bundles of ranks $b-3,b-4$ and fit into a Frobenius-equivariant exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\mathcal K\longrightarrow\mathcal I \xrightarrow{\lambda}\mathcal O_{P^\circ}\longrightarrow0, \qquad \lambda=\delta_1\delta_2s, \] whose quotient has the constant unit Frobenius. Moreover \[ \det\mathcal I=\det\mathcal K=\mathcal O_P(-b),\qquad H^0(P,\mathcal I)=H^0(P,\mathcal K)=0. \] The full coherent Frobenius maps into $\mathcal I$; its restriction there is generically bijective and has the required relative unit Lang system. Its determinant, and the determinant on $\mathcal K$, give the same nonzero homogeneous polynomial $h_d^{\mathrm u}\in H^0(P,\mathcal O_P(b))$, up to a common nonzero constant.

statement: [The intersection-point Hasse divisor] Let $a,e$ be positive odd integers and let $D\in|L^e|$ be a fixed smooth sharp curve. On $P_a=|L^a|$, the divisor $R_D$ parametrizing nonreduced intersections $C\cap D$ is irreducible and reduced, and has degree \[ \deg R_D=18ae+9e^2. \] Its generic member has exactly one intersection of multiplicity two and all other intersections simple. Its Frobenius equation is the determinant on the finite intersection algebra.

statement: [An exact factorization on an odd-component boundary] Let $a\ge3$ and $e\ge1$ be odd, put $d=a+e$, and fix a smooth sharp $D\in|L^e|$. The linear embedding \[ j_D:P_a\hookrightarrow P_d,\qquad C\longmapsto C\cup D \] satisfies, up to a nonzero scalar, \[ j_D^*h_d^{\mathrm u}=h_a\,r_D, \] where $h_a$ is the irreducible reduced odd-degree relative Hasse polynomial and $r_D$ is the irreducible equation of $R_D$ from the preceding lemma. For $a=1$, the same restriction is nonzero and is divisible by $r_D$; no complete factorization in this case is needed below.

statement: [All degrees on the fixed supersingular product] Let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic two, and embed $X=E\times E$, $E:y^2+y=x^3$, by $L=\mathcal O_E(3O)\boxtimes\mathcal O_E(3O)$. For every $d\ge1$, the entire geometric and arithmetic images of the relative mod-two Hasse--Witt local system are \[ G_{\mathrm{geom},d}=G_{\mathrm{arith},d}= \begin{cases} \GL_{9d^2-1}(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ odd},\\[2pt] \mathbf F_2^{\,9d^2-4}\rtimes\GL_{9d^2-4}(\mathbf F_2), &d\text{ even}. \end{cases} \] The even image is the full pointwise stabilizer of the unique nonzero invariant covector in rank $9d^2-3$. The odd system is geometrically irreducible; the even system has its unique proper nonzero invariant subspace of codimension one.

statement: [The mixed first-image sheaf and a natural block] Work over an algebraically closed field, and suppose the odd degree-one image on $X$ is $\GL_8(\mathbf F_2)$. For even $d\ge2$ put $N=L^d$, $W=H^0(N)$, $b=b_d$, $P=\mathbf P(W)$ and $\mathcal B=W^*\otimes\mathcal O_P(-1)$. Normalize invariant derivations $e,n$ so that $e^2=e$, $n^2=0$ and $en=ne$, with $e$ from $E$ and $n$ from $E_0$. They lift canonically to $N$, since $N$ is a Frobenius pullback. Set \[ \mathcal I=\ker\bigl(\mathcal B\xrightarrow{(s,es)}\mathcal O_P^2\bigr), \qquad \mathcal K=\ker\bigl(\mathcal B\xrightarrow{(s,es,ns,ens)}\mathcal O_P^4\bigr). \] There is a closed subset $Z\subset P$, of codimension $b/4$, outside which these are vector bundles and \[ 0\longrightarrow\mathcal K\longrightarrow\mathcal I \xrightarrow{(ns,ens)}\mathcal O_{P\setminus Z}^2 \longrightarrow0 \] is Frobenius-equivariant with constant unit quotient. Their reflexive extensions satisfy \[ \rank\mathcal I=b-2,\quad\rank\mathcal K=b-4,\quad \det\mathcal I=\det\mathcal K=\mathcal O_P(-b),\quad H^0(P,\mathcal I)=H^0(P,\mathcal K)=0. \] Frobenius on $\mathcal I$ is generically bijective, its Lang system is the required relative unit system, and its determinant is a nonzero degree-$b$ form $h_d^{\mathrm u}$. The geometric group contains an actual natural $\GL_8(\mathbf F_2)$ block fixing a complementary subspace. Its natural eight-space lies in the common covector kernel.

Its common covector kernel is irreducible and is contained in every nonzero invariant subspace; the quotient is the trivial two-dimensional representation. In particular the odd systems are geometrically irreducible and the even systems are not.

statement: [Full elementary inertia from a moving kernel line] Let $Y$ be a smooth variety over a perfect field of characteristic two, and let $D\subset Y$ be an integral divisor. Suppose its geometric generic rank is $r$, its stable rank at the generic point of $D$ is $r-1$, its linearized kernel there is a line, and its determinant has order one along $D$. Suppose that on a neighbourhood of the generic point of $D$ there is an inclusion $\mathcal E\subset V\otimes\mathcal O_Y$ as a subbundle of a constant bundle, and the linearized kernel line in $F^*\mathcal E$ defines a rational map \[ \kappa:D\dashrightarrow\mathbf P(V^{(2)}) \] whose differential has rank $r-1$ at the generic point. Then the divisorial inertia image of the generic Lang local system contains the entire elementary group \[ \operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf F_2,\mathbf F_2^{r-1}), \] acting trivially on the regular $(r-1)$-dimensional unit subspace and on the one-dimensional quotient. In particular it contains every transvection with that fixed hyperplane.

statement: [The new hypothesis does not follow from tensor stability] This theorem is conditional. The extra hypothesis is verified for every nonordinary principal surface in Theorem~\ref{thm:every-nonordinary-ppav-degree-one-full-candidate} below; the present argument alone does not verify it on the actual Cartier locus. In particular, stability of the original theta tensor does not suffice by a formal invariant-theory implication. In the four-dimensional Cartan coefficient space, consider \[ \alpha_1^3+\alpha_2^3+\alpha_3^3=0. \] This is an irreducible cubic hypersurface: its plane base is a smooth Fermat cubic in characteristic two. It is not contained in the finite union of reflection hyperplanes. By \citet[Proposition~2.10]{RainsSam2018Trivectors}, its general point therefore defines a stable original tensor, with all $\alpha_i\ne0$. But its polar coefficient $b_0$ is zero, so the polar tensor lies on a coordinate reflection hyperplane and is nonstable by \citet[Proposition~2.9]{RainsSam2018Trivectors}. This proves the failure of the proposed implication on the entire stable Cartan family. It does not identify that hypersurface with any locus of actual Cartier tensors. The subsequent normal-form calculations show that the actual nonordinary Cartier locus satisfies polar stability, and thereby prove the unconditional degree-one fixed-surface theorem without the false general implication.

statement: [Clopen closure of an invariant Lang subgroup] \textup{[Proved under the stated hypotheses; complete independent audits passed.]} Let $B$ be normal, integral and Noetherian, let $E$ be a vector bundle with Frobenius-semilinear map, and let $\mathcal L=\{Fv=v\}$ be its Lang scheme. Suppose $U\subset B$ is a nonempty open where the stable rank is constant, and let $\mathcal S_U\subset\mathcal L_U$ be a finite \etale subgroup local system arising from an invariant $\mathbf F_2$-subspace. Its closure $\overline{\mathcal S}$ in $\mathcal L$ is open and closed and is a subgroup scheme. If $C$ is integral and connected, $C\to B$ meets $U$ generically, and $T\hookrightarrow\mathcal L_C$ is a finite \etale subgroup, then $T\cap\overline{\mathcal S}_C$ is finite \etale of constant rank. If $\mathcal S$ is generically contained in $T$, its entire closure on $C$ is contained in $T$ and retains its generic rank. If $T$ is generically contained in $\mathcal S$, it is contained in the closure on every fibre.

statement: [Proper primitive monodromy in five certified prime types] Let \[ n\in\{5,7,11,13,17\},\qquad m=(n-1)/2. \tag{EDC10} \] For the explicit fixed surface and line \((A,L_m)\) in (EDC1), the nonempty open of smooth curves with maximal relative stable rank has genus \(n+1\), relative rank \(n-1\), and geometric relative Lang image satisfying \[ G_{A,L_m}\ \subseteq\ S_n\ \subsetneq\operatorname{GL}_{n-1}(\mathbf F_2). \tag{EDC11} \] The representation of \(S_n\) is its permutation representation on \(\mathbf F_2^n/\mathbf F_2\mathbf1\). Consequently full linear monodromy fails in each of these actual ample globally generated primitive systems. In particular, the type-\((1,5)\) example has image of order at most \(120\), whereas \(\lvert\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbf F_2)\rvert=20160\).

statement: [Precise relation to the large-degree question] These are completely specified actual geometric counterexamples to an unrestricted full-image assertion for ample globally generated primitive systems. They show that the generic sharp rank theorem and the birational Pfaffian theorem cannot by themselves supply nonzero-Lang connectedness or full primitive image. We have not identified the exact subgroup of \(S_n\) or the theta coefficient ratio of these examples. None of the lines \(L_m\) is very ample: its restriction to an elliptic fibre has degree two and cannot embed that fibre. Moreover the sequence \(L_m\) consists of different primitive polarizations, each retaining fibre degree two. It is not the sequence of powers of a fixed ample embedding line. Accordingly this result does not refute Grothendieck's sufficiently-large hypersurface-degree assertion, does not contradict any proved fixed-principal-cube full-image case, and does not close the general A.4 gate. statement: [Frame component counts under nonproper specialization] Let $B$ be an excellent normal integral scheme, let $U\subset\mathbf P_B(\mathcal W)$ be an open whose geometric fibres are nonempty, and let $\mathcal V$ be a rank-$r$ $\mathbf F_2$ local system on $U$. Write $G_{\bar b}$ and $G_{\bar\eta}$ for its geometric images on a geometric fibre and on the geometric generic fibre. Then \[ |G_{\bar\eta}|\ge |G_{\bar b}|. \] If every geometric-fibre image is, up to conjugation, contained in a fixed subgroup $P\subset\GL_r(\mathbf F_2)$ and one geometric fibre has image $P$, the geometric generic image is $P$. Under the same fixed-subgroup bound, if that equality holds generically, it holds on every geometric fibre over a nonempty open of $B$.

statement: [Constant-rank relative unit systems in ppav families] Let $B$ be reduced and locally Noetherian, and let $A\to B$ be a family of principally polarized abelian surfaces in characteristic two, supplied with a relatively ample line bundle $M$ representing the polarization, and suppose every geometric fibre has the same two-rank $f\in\{0,1\}$. Fix $d\ge1$ and put $b=9d^2$. On the open $U_d$ of smooth curves in $|M^{3d}|$ having maximal relative stable rank, the relative Lang system is a finite etale local system of rank \[ r=\begin{cases}b-1,&d\text{ odd},\\ b-3+f,&d\text{ even}. \end{cases} \] Every geometric fibre of $U_d\to B$ is a nonempty integral open of a projective space. Its geometric image is contained in $\GL_r(\mathbf F_2)$ in odd degree and in the pointwise stabilizer of $f+1$ independent covectors in even degree.

statement: [The needed genus-two strata and their specializations] Over $\overline{\mathbf F}_2$, the two-rank-one stratum of principally polarized abelian surfaces is smooth and irreducible. statement: [Generic full images on nonordinary ppav surfaces] Let $(A,M)$ be a geometric generic principally polarized abelian surface on a two-rank-$f$ stratum, $f\in\{0,1\}$, in characteristic two. For $f=0$ this means the geometric generic point of any irreducible component. For every $d\ge1$, the relative system on the maximal-rank smooth open of the complete linear system $|M^{3d}|$ has \[ G_{\mathrm{geom},d}= \begin{cases} \GL_{9d^2-1}(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ odd},\\[2pt] \operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf F_2^{f+1},\mathbf F_2^{9d^2-4}) \rtimes\GL_{9d^2-4}(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ even}. \end{cases} \] For any perfect field of definition with such geometric generic moduli, the arithmetic image equals the geometric image. For the embedding by $M^3$, the same assertion for ambient degree-$d$ hypersurfaces holds whenever ambient restriction is surjective, in particular for $d\ge\max(1,\operatorname{reg}(\mathcal I_A)-1)$.

statement: [A rank-two Frobenius bundle and its endomorphism quotient] Let $E/\mathbf F_2$ be $y^2+y=x^3$, let $O$ be its point at infinity, and identify its Frobenius twist with $E$ by this model. Write $F$ for relative Frobenius and $\partial x=1$, $\partial y=x^2$ for the invariant vector field. For $q>0$ put \[ V=F_*\OO_E(2qO),\qquad H=\OO_E(qO). \] Then $V\simeq U\otimes H$, where $U=F_*\OO_E$ is the nonsplit extension of $\OO_E$ by itself. There is a perfect alternating pairing $V\otimes V\to\det V\simeq\OO_E(2qO)$, given by Cartier trace with respect to $dx$. Moreover \[ h^0(E,\End V)=2,\qquad h^0\bigl(E,\End V/\OO_E\operatorname{id}\bigr)=2. \] The latter two-dimensional space is spanned by the classes of multiplication by the source function $x$ and of $\partial$.

statement: [A uniform sparse section] For every positive integer $q$ divisible by six, put $N_q=\OO_E(2qO)\boxtimes\OO_E(3O)$ on $E\times E$. In coordinates $(x,y)$ and $(z,w)$ take the section \[ \begin{split} s_q&=A+Bz+Cw,\\ A&=x+P\{x^2+(1+x)y\},\\ B&=x+Py^2,\\ C&=1+Py,\\ P&=x^{q-3}. \end{split} \] All coefficients lie in $\mathbf F_2$. The root-removed Cartier endomorphism $C_{s_q}$ of $H^0(E\times E,N_q)$ satisfies \[ \rank C_{s_q}=\rank C_{s_q}^2=6q-2. \] In particular a general smooth member of $|N_q|$ has full and relative stable rank $6q-2$.

statement: [Cartier bounds from one or two even factors] Let $E:y^2+y=x^3$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, let $A=E\times E$, and put $N=\OO_E(mO)\boxtimes\OO_E(nO)$, where $m,n\ge3$.
